note: This is the last commit confirmed live in production as of this deploy. Update this file after every deploy made THROUGH this pipeline, so the next build's manifest.previous_commit is accurate.
release_contents: Priority 1 recruitment fix + follow-on work: (1) ApplicationDocumentService now scans the first 1024 bytes for %PDF- instead of requiring it at byte 0 — root-cause fix for the production incident where valid PDFs with a BOM or leading whitespace were rejected. (2) job_posting_slugs history table + JobPosting::uniqueSlug(), letting an admin rename a posting's URL slug with the old one permanently 308-redirecting via the site's permanentRedirect(). (3) Dedicated share_image_path on both notices and job_postings (separate from any in-page cover image), admin upload UI with preview/replace/remove, public share-image streaming endpoints, and a 3-tier fallback for a job posting's og:image (own upload -> linked notice's own share image -> linked notice's cover image). (4) A shared socialMeta() helper on the Next.js site fixing 13 pages that defined openGraph without twitter and silently inherited the root layout's org Twitter card. (5) Type guards widened to accept share_image_url being absent (not just null) for cross-deploy safety between the two independently-deployed apps.
migrations_applied: Both migrations for this release applied via migrate-apply after reviewing migrate-check's pretend_output: 2026_09_20_090000_create_job_posting_slugs_table (659.44ms) and 2026_09_20_100000_add_share_image_to_notices_and_job_postings (9.25ms). Both purely additive (new table; two nullable columns) — no drops, no backfills. pending_migrations_detected was true beforehand and false-equivalent (nothing left) after.
switch_note: Clean switch: ok:true, atomic_rename_ms 0.452, public_asset_sync_ms 11.3, switched_at 2026-09-20T12:00:03+00:00. config:clear/view:clear/config:cache/view:cache all exit 0. route:cache correctly RAN (routes_changed true — this release touched routes/api.php and routes/web.php for the new share-image and slug-history endpoints).
smoke_test_live: ok:true. /login 200, /forgot-password 200, /admin 302 (unauthenticated redirect, expected). app_debug false. log_size_bytes_after_switch 0 (no errors logged since switch).
production_qa_evidence: A disposable JobPosting (title 'PROD QA DISPOSABLE DELETE ME', never linked to any real notice or user) was created directly against production via a self-deleting one-shot script (never left in the public docroot beyond its own single invocation), verified, and fully deleted again in the same session — no real user data was read, written, or touched. Verified against LIVE production: (a) old-slug -> new-slug 308 redirect for both the detail and /apply routes; (b) full share-image + Twitter/OG metadata tag set on the recruitment detail page, og:image absolute and pointing at admin.provatferi.org; (c) the share-image endpoint returns 200, Content-Type image/jpeg, real JPEG magic bytes, and leaks no private storage path/UUID in any response header; (d) two real disposable applications submitted with a real photo AND the exact BOM-header and leading-whitespace PDFs that the original incident's root cause affects — both correctly accepted (201, VOL-2026-0001 and VOL-2026-0005) with photo_path/cv_path both present and confirmed to actually exist on the private disk (the Admin-visibility proof, read directly rather than by rotating the Super Admin password); (e) full cleanup verified — posting, slug history, both applications and their stored files all confirmed gone, backend API returns 404 for both slugs post-cleanup.
known_cosmetic_cache_artifact: For a few minutes after deleting the disposable fixture, provatferi.org still rendered a stale cached copy of the old/new-slug recruitment pages (visiting them mid-QA had already populated Next.js's own in-process ISR fetch cache, which hosting_clearWebsiteCacheV1's Hostinger-CDN purge does not reach). Confirmed via the direct backend API that the underlying data was correctly gone (404 on both slugs) at the same moment the cached HTML still rendered — this is a transient cache-layer artifact, not a data or logic defect, and the page only ever showed the disposable QA placeholder title, never real applicant data. It self-expires on Next.js's normal revalidate window.
cdn_purge_note: Both provatferi.org and admin.provatferi.org purged via clearWebsiteCache after the institutional Node.js build; provatferi.org purged a second time after disposable-fixture cleanup. Each request returned {message:'Request accepted'} (acknowledges the request, not propagation) — verified separately via plain-vs-cache-busted byte-identical responses (62763 bytes) and via the direct backend API for the post-cleanup state.
cron_timing_note: Cron runs in UTC; server Date header matched local UTC clock exactly this release. One-shot crons scheduled 5-6 minutes ahead on specific minutes (never `* * * * *`), read once, then deleted immediately — cron slate confirmed empty before arming each next step. Margins used: ~90s for fast commands (stage, contract-check, migrate-check, migrate-apply, smoke-test-live), ~8min for build (server-side composer install) and smoke-test-isolated/switch.
switch_gate_note: release-manager.php `switch` requires stage/build/contract_check/smoke_test_isolated but NOT migrate_apply, even when migrate-check reported pending migrations. Always read migrate-check yourself and run migrate-apply before scheduling switch; never pre-schedule switch on a release that carries unreviewed migrations. Followed correctly this release: migrate-check's pretend_output was read and matched the two known-additive local migrations exactly before migrate-apply ran.
